question: Do the three production scalar-twist obstruction blocks share one elliptic norm obstruction, and can their scalar gluing produce the genus-two object present in the cyclic small control?
inputs: Frozen integral cubics and CT matrices for production cases 0,4,5; frozen generic-adapted symplectic masks; the small cyclic cubic control.
checks: Certify each production cubic is irreducible with nonsquare discriminant. Enumerate the Galois-equivariant invertible maps on E[2] for S3 and C3. Verify all retained symplectic block masks. Independently check the twist isomorphism, Weil restriction equations, and integer isogeny/polarization matrices.
hypothesis_test: A nonstandard rational 2-torsion identification would leave a smooth genus-two scalar gluing open. A singleton centralizer excludes that route. Nondegenerate CT blocks give lower bounds for the local-global elliptic norm defect, not new ranks.
boundary: The geometric gate uses equations only. CT block sizes use retrospective rational witnesses and cannot enter prospective selection as point-independent features. No new CT pairing, global norm equation, class group, descent, or search is computed.
